greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. We gather today in the presence of the Lord, seeking the comfort of His Word and the strength of His promise.
penitential: Lord, you are the healer of every broken heart, Lord have mercy. Christ, you are the light that shines in the darkness, Christ have mercy. Lord, you are our hope in this life and the next, Lord have mercy.
psalm_response: Lord, let your face shine on me.
homily:
We often think of the spiritual life as a ladder we are meant to climb. We imagine that if we are smart enough, if we are diligent enough, or if we simply find the right set of instructions, we can ascend to the heights of understanding. We want to map out the mysteries of our lives just as we map out the geography of a new city. We want to know why the path turns where it does, why the sun sets so early on some days, and why, when we are looking for a clear sky, we find ourselves walking through the thick, grey fog of grief.

Look at Job in our first reading today. He is a man who has been stripped of everything he called his own. He has lost his children, his wealth, his health, and his sense of how the world is supposed to work. He sits in the dust, and he challenges the heavens. He demands an explanation. And how does God respond? He does not give Job a lecture on theology. He does not provide a list of reasons. He simply asks Job if he was there when the foundations of the earth were laid. He asks him if he can command the morning. And in that moment, Job stops talking. He says, 'I have dealt with great things that I do not understand; things too wonderful for me, which I cannot know.' He stops trying to solve the mystery, and instead, he begins to behold the Mystery. He says, 'I had heard of you by word of mouth, but now my eye has seen you.'

There is a profound, quiet shift in that sentence. Job moves from hearing about God to seeing Him. And he sees Him right there in the ashes. He realizes that the Creator is not distant; He is intimate. He is the one who sustains the breath in his lungs, even when those lungs are heavy with sorrow. Job’s life is not a tragedy that ends in the dust; it is a story that is redeemed by the presence of the One who never left his side.

I want you to think about Benjamin Vo. You know the facet of him I want to touch today: his deep, unshakeable love for his family—the way he was always, quietly, looking out for you, Alan, and for you, Thao, and for his brother, Ryan. You remember how he would look at the world with that brilliant, analytical mind, always coding, always dreaming, always planning. But beneath that intellect was a heart that was so profoundly soft. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his Uncle William. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, he didn't need to make a show of his kindness. He simply offered. That offer was a prayer. It was the movement of a soul that was already living in the Kingdom of God, where the currency is not gold, but the total gift of oneself. That is the kind of boy Benjamin was. He was a boy who understood that the true measure of a life is not how much you gather, but how much you are willing to give.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these past three months, the world has felt like it has lost its map. You remember the way he would look at you, Alan, with such pride, as if you were the architect of his whole world. You remember the way he would giggle when he talked about 'con chim airlines.' That was a sound of pure, unadulterated joy. It wasn't just a dream of airplanes; it was the sound of a spirit that was meant for the heights. And now, he has reached the destination he was always pointing toward. He is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is standing in the presence of the Father, and he is seeing the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

There is a temptation, when we are grieving, to think that we have been left behind in the dark. We feel the absence of the smile, the silence of the morning greeting, the empty chair at the table. But the Gospel today gives us a different perspective. Jesus says to his disciples, 'Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.' He is talking about the revelation of the Father. He is talking about the gift of seeing the world not as a collection of random events, but as a story held in the hands of God. He says, 'I give you praise, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for although you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned, you have revealed them to the childlike.'

Benjamin was one of those children. He had that rare, beautiful capacity to be both brilliant and childlike—to hold the complexity of the world in his mind and the simplicity of trust in his heart. When he looked at you, he didn't see a 'what if' or a 'why.' He saw his parents. He saw his home. He saw the people he loved, and he loved them without reservation. That is the grace you gave him, and that is the grace he is now reflecting back to you from the presence of God. You did not miss anything. You were the sanctuary he needed. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You are not being accused by his absence; you are being held by his love.

Ryan, you are the one who carries that peace now. You are the brother who knows the rhythm of Ben’s heart. You know the secrets of the games he coded, the joy he found in the simple things, the way he looked at the world with wonder. When you walk into a room, you are carrying that legacy. You are carrying the curiosity, the kindness, and the love that you and Ben shared. You are not a brother who is walking alone. You are a brother who is walking with the strength of a love that has already arrived at the destination. Keep being the boy who is curious. Keep being the brother who knows that love is the only thing that actually lasts. You are a family of four, and that will never change. You are just living in two different rooms of the same house, and the door between them is held open by the grace of Christ.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that sometimes visits you in the quiet of the night. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of 'what if' or 'did I miss something.' I want to lift that stone from you today. Illness is never a punishment, and it is never the fault of those who loved and cared for the one who suffered. God does not send sickness, and He does not look at your care for Benjamin and find it lacking. You were his world. You were his comfort. You were the ones who stood by him through every storm. You did not miss anything. You are not to blame. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what you are doing. You are taking the love that was poured into Ben, and you are letting it flow into the lives of others. You are ensuring that his life is not a closed chapter, but a living, breathing, life-sustaining force. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to forgive, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

We are on this earth, as the Psalm says, to see the bounty of the Lord in the land of the living. Sometimes that land feels like a desert. Sometimes it feels like we are waiting for a harvest that will never come. But the Gospel tells us that we are watched over. We are guarded. We are guided. We are never out of the sight of the Father. When the days feel long and the silence feels heavy, remember that you are not being asked to understand the mysteries of the universe. You are being asked to trust the One who holds the stars in place and who holds Benjamin in the palm of His hand. You are being asked to live in such a way that his memory continues to be a blessing to everyone you meet.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that God may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of the Resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Job answered the LORD and said:I know that you can do all things,
and that no purpose of yours can be hindered.
I have dealt with great things that I do not understand;
things too wonderful for me, which I cannot know.
I had heard of you by word of mouth,
but now my eye has seen you.
Therefore I disown what I have said,
and repent in dust and ashes.Thus the LORD blessed the latter days of Job
more than his earlier ones.
For he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels,
a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
And he had seven sons and three daughters,
of whom he called the first Jemimah,
the second Keziah, and the third Kerenhappuch.
In all the land no other women were as beautiful
as the daughters of Job;
and their father gave them an inheritance
along with their brothers.
After this, Job lived a hundred and forty years;
and he saw his children, his grandchildren,
and even his great-grandchildren.
Then Job died, old and full of years.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (135) Lord, let your face shine on me.
Teach me wisdom and knowledge,
for in your commands I trust.
R. Lord, let your face shine on me.
It is good for me that I have been afflicted,
that I may learn your statutes.
R. Lord, let your face shine on me.
I know, O LORD, that your ordinances are just,
and in your faithfulness you have afflicted me.
R. Lord, let your face shine on me.
According to your ordinances they still stand firm:
all things serve you.
R. Lord, let your face shine on me.
I am your servant; give me discernment
that I may know your decrees.
R. Lord, let your face shine on me.
The revelation of your words sheds light,
giving understanding to the simple.
R. Lord, let your face shine on me.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
The seventy-two disciples returned rejoicing and said to Jesus,
“Lord, even the demons are subject to us because of your name.”
Jesus said, “I have observed Satan fall like lightning from the sky.
Behold, I have given you the power
‘to tread upon serpents’ and scorpions
and upon the full force of the enemy
and nothing will harm you.
Nevertheless, do not rejoice because the spirits are subject to you,
but rejoice because your names are written in heaven.”At that very moment he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said,
“I give you praise, Father, Lord of heaven and earth,
for although you have hidden these things
from the wise and the learned
you have revealed them to the childlike.
Yes, Father, such has been your gracious will.
All things have been handed over to me by my Father.
No one knows who the Son is except the Father,
and who the Father is except the Son
and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.”Turning to the disciples in private he said,
“Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I say to you,
many prophets and kings desired to see what you see,
but did not see it,
and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.”

day: Saturday of the Twenty-sixth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.
